X.assistant:
For proper chip-shop-style chips, **fry them twice**: first to cook the middle, then to crisp the outside. That’s the bit worth fussing over. ([bbcgoodfood.com](https://www.bbcgoodfood.com/videos/techniques/how-make-chips-video))

- **Use floury potatoes**, such as Maris Piper, and cut them evenly so they cook at the same rate. ([bbcgoodfood.com](https://www.bbcgoodfood.com/videos/techniques/how-make-chips-video))
- **First fry: 130°C**, roughly 7–8 minutes, until cooked through but still pale. Drain and leave to cool before the second fry. ([bbcgoodfood.com](https://www.bbcgoodfood.com/videos/techniques/how-make-chips-video))
- **Second fry: 180°C**, until golden and crisp. Work in small batches—crowding the fryer drops the oil temperature. ([bbcgoodfood.com](https://www.bbcgoodfood.com/videos/techniques/how-make-chips-video))
- **Salt after frying, not before**, and serve straight away. ([breville.com](https://www.breville.com/content/dam/breville/au/assets/miscellaneous/instruction-manual/woks-skillets-deep-fryers/BDF500-instruction-manual.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Use a thermometer or temperature-controlled fryer, and don’t leave the hot oil unattended. Dinner should have drama, but not that much. ([git.macropus.org](https://git.macropus.org/bbc-food/www.bbc.co.uk/food/recipes/thebestchipsyouhavee_93121.html?utm_source=openai))
X.person: Any tips to make the chips really good?

X.assistant:
**Yes—a deep, heavy-based pan works.** Same frying principle, but you control the oil temperature yourself rather than relying on a thermostat. A frying thermometer is the useful bit of kit here. ([greatbritishchefs.com](https://www.greatbritishchefs.com/how-to-cook/deep-fry-without-deep-fat-fryer?utm_source=openai))

- **Fill it no more than one-third with oil**, leaving room for bubbling and the chips. ([greatbritishchefs.com](https://www.greatbritishchefs.com/how-to-cook/deep-fry-without-deep-fat-fryer?utm_source=openai))
- **Dry the cut chips thoroughly** before lowering them gently into the oil—water makes hot oil spit. ([sainthelena.gov.sh](https://www.sainthelena.gov.sh/documents/chip-pan-safety-advice-2/?utm_source=openai))
- **Keep the two-stage fry:** about 130°C until tender and pale, then cool them before frying at 180°C until golden. Small batches keep the temperature from dropping too far. ([bbcgoodfood.com](https://www.bbcgoodfood.com/videos/techniques/how-make-chips-video?utm_source=openai))
- **Stay beside the pan throughout.** If the oil starts smoking, turn off the heat and let it cool. If it catches fire, never add water or move the pan; turn off the heat only if safe, get out and call the fire service. ([sainthelena.gov.sh](https://www.sainthelena.gov.sh/documents/chip-pan-safety-advice-2/?utm_source=openai))
X.person: I don't have a fryer, just a deep pan. Does that work the same?

Y.assistant: Do you mean fries/chunky chips, thin potato chips, or tortilla chips—and are you frying, baking, or air-frying them?
Y.person: Any tips to make the chips really good?

Y.assistant:
The biggest trick is to fry them twice: gently to cook the middle, then hotter to crisp the outside, with a cooling break between. ([bbcgoodfood.com](https://www.bbcgoodfood.com/videos/techniques/how-make-chips-video))

1. Cut them evenly, and dry them thoroughly before they go anywhere near the oil—wet potatoes make it spit. ([bbcgoodfood.com](https://www.bbcgoodfood.com/videos/techniques/how-make-chips-video))
2. First fry at 130°C for roughly 7–8 minutes, until cooked through but still pale. Thick chips may need longer; go by tenderness rather than the clock. Lift out, drain and leave to cool. You can do this stage ahead. ([bbcgoodfood.com](https://www.bbcgoodfood.com/videos/techniques/how-make-chips-video))
3. Second fry at 180°C until golden and crisp. Drain and serve straight away. ([bbcgoodfood.com](https://www.bbcgoodfood.com/videos/techniques/how-make-chips-video))
4. Work in small batches. Crowding the pan drops the oil temperature and can leave the chips greasy. ([leithsonline.com](https://www.leithsonline.com/post/the-rules-of-deep-fat-frying))

For your pan: never fill it more than one-third full of oil, stay beside it, and turn the heat off if the oil smokes. Don’t move a pan of hot oil. ([manchesterfire.gov.uk](https://manchesterfire.gov.uk/your-safety/home-fire-safety/cooking-safety/deep-frying-with-oil/))

Have you got a cooking thermometer that can measure frying temperatures?
Y.person: Proper chunky chips, frying them. I've got a deep pan but no fryer, and floury potatoes.

Y.assistant:
A small cube of white bread gives a rough check: if it browns in about 30 seconds, the oil is roughly 180–190°C—hot enough for the second, crisping fry. Lower it in carefully with a dry utensil, rather than dropping it from a height. It’s a guide, not a reliable temperature measurement. ([origin.ckbk.com](https://origin.ckbk.com/reference/cook52062c03s001ss012e005/deep-frying-fish-in-batter?utm_source=openai))

That test won’t reliably identify the gentler 130°C first fry. For controlling both stages, a thermometer rated for deep-frying is the better option; don’t treat the bread test as an exact substitute. ([ask.fsis.usda.gov](https://ask.fsis.usda.gov/article/What-are-deep-fry-thermometers?utm_source=openai))

Never wait for smoke: if it starts smoking, switch off the heat and leave the pan to cool without moving it. Keep the pan no more than one-third full, dry your chips thoroughly, and never test oil with water. If it catches fire, don’t move it or pour water on it—get out and call the fire service. ([lafd.org](https://lafd.org/cooking-safety?utm_source=openai))
Y.person: Not sure I've got one. How can I tell when the oil's hot enough without it?
